title: Mark Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Mark chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Mark Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Mark Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Mark 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus taking Peter, James, and John up a mountain
The appearance of Elias and Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus taking Peter, James, and John up a mountain
questions.explanation: This event is mentioned in Mark 9:2, which is the first significant action described.

questions.question: Who did Jesus take with him up into the high mountain?
questions.correctAnswer: Peter, James, and John
questions.explanation: This is stated in Mark 9:2 where it mentions that Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him.

questions.question: What happened to Jesus' raiment during the transfiguration?
options: It became shining, exceeding white as snow
questions.correctAnswer: It became shining, exceeding white as snow
questions.explanation: Mark 9:3 describes how Jesus' raiment became shining and white as snow.

questions.question: Which two figures appeared with Jesus during the transfiguration?
questions.correctAnswer: Elias and Moses
questions.explanation: Mark 9:4 states that Elias and Moses appeared and were talking with Jesus.

questions.question: What did Peter suggest making while on the mountain?
questions.correctAnswer: Three tabernacles
questions.explanation: In Mark 9:5, Peter suggested making three tabernacles, one for Jesus, one for Moses, and one for Elias.

questions.question: Why did Peter not know what to say?
questions.correctAnswer: They were sore afraid
questions.explanation: Mark 9:6 explains that Peter did not know what to say because they were sore afraid.

questions.question: What overshadowed them during the transfiguration?
questions.correctAnswer: A cloud
questions.explanation: Mark 9:7 mentions that there was a cloud that overshadowed them.

questions.question: What did the voice from the cloud say?
options: This is my beloved Son: hear him
This is my servant: follow him
This is my chosen one: trust him
This is my friend: believe him
questions.correctAnswer: This is my beloved Son: hear him
questions.explanation: The voice from the cloud states in Mark 9:7, 'This is my beloved Son: hear him.'

questions.question: What did the disciples see when they looked around after the voice spoke?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus only
questions.explanation: Mark 9:8 confirms that they saw no man anymore, save Jesus only with themselves.

questions.question: What did Jesus charge the disciples when they came down from the mountain?
options: To tell everyone what they saw
To tell no man what they had seen
questions.correctAnswer: To tell no man what they had seen
questions.explanation: In Mark 9:9, Jesus charged them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of man were risen from the dead.

questions.question: What were the disciples questioning among themselves?
options: What the rising from the dead should mean
questions.correctAnswer: What the rising from the dead should mean
questions.explanation: Mark 9:10 indicates that they were questioning one another about what the rising from the dead should mean.

questions.question: True or False: Elias must first come according to the scribes.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Mark 9:11 shows that the disciples asked Jesus why the scribes said that Elias must first come.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told the disciples that Elias had indeed come.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Mark 9:13, Jesus confirms that Elias is indeed come.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples saw a multitude of people before they met Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Mark 9:14 states that a great multitude was around the disciples when Jesus came to them, not that they saw a multitude before meeting him.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus asked the scribes what they were questioning about.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Mark 9:16 shows that Jesus asked the scribes what question they were with the disciples about, not just any questioning.

medium.title: Mark Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Mark Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the father of the child cry out to Jesus?
options: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
I have faith in you, Lord.
I wish to see my son well.
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
questions.explanation: This is the direct quote from Mark 9:24, where the father expresses his belief yet acknowledges his struggles with unbelief.

questions.question: What does Mark 9:23 promise will happen if someone believes?
options: All things are possible to him that believeth.
questions.correctAnswer: All things are possible to him that believeth.
questions.explanation: This is stated in Mark 9:23, emphasizing the power of belief in the context of Jesus’ healing.

questions.question: What was the condition of the child brought to Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: He had a dumb spirit.
questions.explanation: This is found in Mark 9:17, where the father describes the condition of his son.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the foul spirit in Mark 9:25?
options: Come out of him, and enter no more into him.
questions.correctAnswer: Come out of him, and enter no more into him.
questions.explanation: This command is given directly in Mark 9:25 as Jesus rebukes the spirit.

questions.question: What did Jesus teach his disciples about the kind of spirit that could come out only by prayer and fasting?
options: It is a spirit of doubt.
It is a spirit of disobedience.
This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.
It is a spirit of anger.
questions.correctAnswer: This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.
questions.explanation: This is stated in Mark 9:29, highlighting the necessity of prayer and fasting for certain spiritual challenges.

questions.question: How did the crowd react when they saw Jesus after he came down from the mountain?
questions.correctAnswer: They were greatly amazed.
questions.explanation: Mark 9:15 describes the crowd's reaction to Jesus' presence as one of amazement.

questions.question: What question did Jesus ask his disciples in Mark 9:33?
options: What were you discussing on the way?
Who do you say that I am?
questions.correctAnswer: What were you discussing on the way?
questions.explanation: This question is found in Mark 9:33 as Jesus inquires about their conversation.

questions.question: What was the main theme of Jesus' teaching in Mark 9:31?
options: He will rise again on the third day.
questions.correctAnswer: He will rise again on the third day.
questions.explanation: Mark 9:31 mentions that Jesus foretold his death and resurrection to his disciples.

questions.question: What did the disciples fail to understand according to Mark 9:32?
questions.correctAnswer: The significance of his resurrection.
questions.explanation: Mark 9:32 states that they did not understand Jesus' prediction of his resurrection.

questions.question: What were the disciples disputing among themselves according to Mark 9:34?
options: Who would be the first to believe.
questions.correctAnswer: Who should be the greatest.
questions.explanation: This is mentioned in Mark 9:34, where the disciples remained silent about their dispute over greatness.

questions.question: What did the father ask Jesus to do for his son in Mark 9:22?
options: Have compassion on us, and help us.
questions.correctAnswer: Have compassion on us, and help us.
questions.explanation: This plea is expressed by the father in Mark 9:22, indicating his desperation for help.

questions.question: What action did Jesus take after the spirit came out of the boy according to Mark 9:27?
options: He took him by the hand and lifted him up.
He told him to go home.
questions.correctAnswer: He took him by the hand and lifted him up.
questions.explanation: This is documented in Mark 9:27, showing Jesus' compassion and authority.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus expressed frustration with the faith of the disciples.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Mark 9:19, Jesus addresses the faithlessness of the generation, implying frustration with those who lack faith, including his disciples.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus encouraged the father of the child to have doubt.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jesus encouraged belief, stating that all things are possible to him that believeth (Mark 9:23).

questions.question: True or False: The disciples were able to cast out the spirit without prayer and fasting.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jesus stated in Mark 9:29 that this kind can come forth only by prayer and fasting, indicating the necessity of those practices.

hard.title: Mark Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Mark Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to Mark 9:35, what must a person be if they desire to be first?
options: Last of all and servant of all
Teacher and leader of the twelve
questions.correctAnswer: Last of all and servant of all
questions.explanation: Mark 9:35 states, 'If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all.'

questions.question: In Mark 9:36, whom did Jesus take and set in the midst of the disciples?
questions.correctAnswer: A child
questions.explanation: Mark 9:36 says, 'And he took a child, and set him in the midst of them.'

questions.question: What does receiving a child in Jesus' name signify according to Mark 9:37?
options: Receiving Jesus and Him that sent Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Receiving Jesus and Him that sent Jesus
questions.explanation: Mark 9:37 says, 'Whosoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.'

questions.question: Why did John say they forbade a man casting out devils in Jesus’ name in Mark 9:38?
questions.correctAnswer: Because he followeth not us
questions.explanation: Mark 9:38 records John saying, 'we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him.'

questions.question: What reason does Jesus give in Mark 9:39 for not forbidding those who do miracles in His name but do not follow them?
options: There is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me
questions.correctAnswer: There is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me
questions.explanation: Mark 9:39 states, 'Forbid him not: for there is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me.'

questions.question: According to Mark 9:41, what will happen to whoever gives a cup of water to drink in Jesus' name?
options: He shall not lose his reward
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not lose his reward
questions.explanation: Mark 9:41 says, 'verily I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'offendō' (offend) in Mark 9:42 mean?
options: To cause to stumble or sin
questions.correctAnswer: To cause to stumble or sin
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'offendō' used in Mark 9:42 means 'to cause to stumble or sin,' especially in a spiritual or moral sense.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Mark 9:43-48 where Jesus talks about cutting off hand, foot, or plucking out eye?
questions.correctAnswer: Hyperbole
questions.explanation: Mark 9:43-48 uses hyperbole, an exaggerated statement to emphasize the seriousness of avoiding sin.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in Mark 9:44, 46, and 48 regarding 'where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched'?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 66:24
questions.explanation: Mark 9:44, 46, 48 quotes Isaiah 66:24 which describes unquenchable fire and undying worm as judgment imagery.

questions.question: Mark 9:1 mentions some standing there will not taste death before seeing the kingdom of God come with power. Which New Testament passage fulfills this promise with the Transfiguration?
questions.correctAnswer: Mark 9:2-8
questions.explanation: Mark 9:2-8 describes the Transfiguration where Jesus is transformed and the kingdom of God is revealed in power, fulfilling Mark 9:1's promise.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus’ teaching on humility in Mark 9:35?
options: The disciples disputing among themselves about who is the greatest
The healing of the mute spirit child
questions.correctAnswer: The disciples disputing among themselves about who is the greatest
questions.explanation: Mark 9:33-34 shows the disciples disputing who should be greatest immediately before Jesus' teaching in 9:35.

questions.question: In Mark 9:29, Jesus says 'This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.' What is the significance of 'fasting' in the original Greek context?
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual discipline to strengthen faith
questions.explanation: The Greek understanding of fasting here emphasizes self-denial as a spiritual discipline to empower prayer, per Mark 9:29.

questions.question: Which typology is illustrated by Jesus taking a child in Mark 9:36-37?
options: Child as a symbol of humility and dependence
Child as a symbol of royalty
Child as a symbol of sacrifice
Child as a symbol of wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Child as a symbol of humility and dependence
questions.explanation: Jesus uses the child to symbolize humility and dependence, qualities necessary for receiving the kingdom (Mark 9:36-37).

questions.question: True or False: According to Mark 9:40, Jesus says, 'He that is not against us is on our part.'
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Mark 9:40 clearly states, 'For he that is not against us is on our part.'

questions.question: True or False: Jesus commanded in Mark 9:43-48 that one must literally cut off their hand, foot, or pluck out their eye to avoid hell.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Mark 9:43-48 uses hyperbolic language to stress avoiding sin, not literal amputation.

theological.title: Mark Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Mark Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Mark 9:1 teach about the kingdom of God?
options: The kingdom of God will be revealed with power to some living disciples
The kingdom of God is purely spiritual and invisible
The kingdom of God is only for the afterlife
The kingdom of God excludes the Jewish people
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom of God will be revealed with power to some living disciples
questions.explanation: Mark 9:1 states that some standing there will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God come with power, indicating a present and powerful manifestation of God's reign.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's suffering and exaltation is taught in Mark 9:12?
options: The Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected before restoration
The Son of Man will rule without suffering or rejection
Elijah will restore all things without any suffering
The Son of Man’s mission is only earthly political restoration
questions.correctAnswer: The Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected before restoration
questions.explanation: Mark 9:12 explains that Elijah comes first to restore all things, but it is also written that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected, revealing the necessity of Christ’s passion before exaltation.

questions.question: What doctrine about faith and divine power is taught in Mark 9:23?
options: All things are possible to him that believes
Faith alone is insufficient for miracles
Only the disciples have power to heal
Power comes from ritual, not faith
questions.correctAnswer: All things are possible to him that believes
questions.explanation: In Mark 9:23, Jesus teaches that if one can believe, all things are possible to the believer, emphasizing the central role of faith in accessing divine power.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Mark 9:19 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: Jesus’ rebuke of the 'faithless generation' in Mark 9:19 reveals God’s longsuffering nature, showing His patient endurance despite human unbelief.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Mark 9:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: The voice from the cloud in Mark 9:7 declaring Jesus as the beloved Son commands reverence and obedience, demonstrating God's holiness and authoritative revelation.

questions.question: How does the transfiguration event in Mark 9:2–8 connect to the broader biblical theme of revelation?
options: It prefigures the glorification of Christ and confirms His divine sonship as foretold in the Old Testament
It denies the Old Testament prophets and replaces them with Jesus alone
It emphasizes only Jesus’ humanity without divine nature
It reveals that Jesus’ kingdom is purely political
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the glorification of Christ and confirms His divine sonship as foretold in the Old Testament
questions.explanation: Mark 9:2–8 shows Jesus’ transfiguration with Moses and Elijah, fulfilling Old Testament prophecy and revealing His divine glory, linking prophecy and fulfillment.

questions.question: How does Mark 9:31–32 prepare for the Gospel’s passion narrative?
options: It announces the Son of Man’s suffering, death, and resurrection, preparing the disciples for the salvific purpose of Jesus’ mission
It focuses only on Jesus’ miracles and omits suffering
It denies Jesus’ resurrection and only highlights His death
It predicts immediate political victory without suffering
questions.correctAnswer: It announces the Son of Man’s suffering, death, and resurrection, preparing the disciples for the salvific purpose of Jesus’ mission
questions.explanation: Mark 9:31–32 teaches that Jesus must be delivered, killed, and rise again on the third day, foreshadowing the passion and resurrection central to salvation history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Mark 9:42 and Mark 9:43 teach about sin and holiness?
options: Sin’s seriousness demands radical personal holiness even at great cost
Sin is minor and easily overlooked
Holiness is optional in the Christian life
God tolerates sin among believers without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Sin’s seriousness demands radical personal holiness even at great cost
questions.explanation: Mark 9:42 warns against offending believers, and 9:43 commands drastic action against sin, teaching that sin’s gravity requires serious measures for holiness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Mark 9:1 and Mark 9:50 teach about the kingdom and Christian life?
options: The kingdom comes with power and believers must live with spiritual seasoning and peace
The kingdom is delayed indefinitely and Christians need not peace
The kingdom is only future and salt is irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom comes with power and believers must live with spiritual seasoning and peace
questions.explanation: Mark 9:1 speaks of the coming kingdom with power, and 9:50 commands Christians to have salt and peace, linking kingdom reality with sanctified life.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Mark 9:35 and Mark 9:37 teach about greatness in God’s kingdom?
options: True greatness is servant-hood and receiving the humble in Christ’s name
Greatness is measured by power and status
Excluding children from the community is required
Only the Jewish elite are truly great
questions.correctAnswer: True greatness is servant-hood and receiving the humble in Christ’s name
questions.explanation: Mark 9:35 teaches the greatest shall be servant of all, and 9:37 shows receiving children is receiving Christ, emphasizing humility and service as kingdom greatness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Mark 9:28-29 teaches that fasting is a magical formula for exorcisms. What does Mark 9:28-29 actually teach?
options: Certain spiritual powers require prayer and fasting for effective spiritual authority
Any exorcism can be done without spiritual preparation
Fasting is irrelevant to spiritual ministry
Jesus taught exorcisms are purely human efforts
questions.correctAnswer: Certain spiritual powers require prayer and fasting for effective spiritual authority
questions.explanation: Mark 9:29 states ‘This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting,’ indicating spiritual disciplines empower ministry rather than magical formulas.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine revelation and authority is taught in Mark 9:38-40?
options: God’s work through others in Jesus’ name is valid and should not be forbidden
Only Jesus’ immediate followers can perform miracles
Miracles done outside the church are from evil
Divine authority is exclusive to one group
questions.correctAnswer: God’s work through others in Jesus’ name is valid and should not be forbidden
questions.explanation: Mark 9:38-40 teaches that those casting out demons in Jesus’ name, though not disciples, are not enemies and should not be forbidden, showing God’s inclusive work.

questions.question: What doctrine about suffering and restoration is taught in Mark 9:13 and Mark 9:12?
options: Elijah came first suffering rejection, prefiguring Christ’s suffering and restoration
Elijah’s coming guarantees immediate political restoration
Only Christ suffers, Elijah’s role is symbolic
questions.correctAnswer: Elijah came first suffering rejection, prefiguring Christ’s suffering and restoration
questions.explanation: Mark 9:13 confirms Elijah indeed came and was mistreated, paralleling Mark 9:12’s teaching on Christ’s suffering as part of the restoration plan.

questions.question: What doctrine about sin’s eternal consequences is taught in Mark 9:44 and Mark 9:48?
options: Hell’s fire is eternal and unquenchable, with ongoing punishment
Hell is a temporary state with eventual annihilation
Hell is symbolic and not literal
There is no punishment after death
questions.correctAnswer: Hell’s fire is eternal and unquenchable, with ongoing punishment
questions.explanation: Mark 9:44 and 9:48 describe hell where 'their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched,' teaching eternal conscious punishment.

questions.question: What doctrine about prayer and spiritual authority is taught in Mark 9:29 and Mark 9:23?
options: Faith, prayer, and fasting are essential for engaging spiritual power effectively
Miracles happen independent of faith or prayer
Power is inherent in people without divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: Faith, prayer, and fasting are essential for engaging spiritual power effectively
questions.explanation: Mark 9:23 emphasizes faith’s power, while 9:29 highlights prayer and fasting as necessary, teaching these as means to spiritual authority.
